fields.claim_quote: Then $e$ is a [[Definition:Bridge (Graph Theory)|bridge]] of minimum [[Definition:Weight (Network Theory)|weight]] in $G$ {{iff}} $e$ belongs to every [[Definition:Minimum Spanning Tree|minimum spanning tree]] of $G$.
fields.explanation: All source hypotheses hold, including pairwise-distinct edge weights 1,2,3. The original triangle has a unique minimum spanning tree of weight 3 containing edge 01. Deleting 01 leaves a connected graph, so the edge is not a graph-theoretic bridge and hence cannot be a minimum-weight bridge. The counterexample refutes the theorem statement; the corresponding proof section is explicitly absent.
fields.flaw: The right-to-left implication of the stated biconditional says that an edge in every minimum spanning tree is a bridge of minimum weight. This implication is false for the original weighted triangle. The {{proof wanted}} marker is not the challenged mathematical passage.
fields.problem:
Title: Edge is Minimum Weight Bridge iff in All Minimum Spanning Trees

Let $G$ be an [[Definition:Undirected Network|undirected network]].

Let every [[Definition:Edge of Graph|edge]] of $G$ have a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] [[Definition:Weight (Network Theory)|weight]].

Let $e$ be an [[Definition:Edge of Graph|edge]] of $G$.

Then $e$ is a [[Definition:Bridge (Graph Theory)|bridge]] of minimum [[Definition:Weight (Network Theory)|weight]] in $G$ {{iff}} $e$ belongs to every [[Definition:Minimum Spanning Tree|minimum spanning tree]] of $G$.

fields.witness: Undirected connected triangle with vertices {0,1,2} and weighted edges 01↦1, 12↦2, 02↦3. Let e=01. The three spanning trees are {01,12}, {01,02}, {12,02}, with weights 3, 4, 5. Thus {01,12} is the unique minimum spanning tree, so e belongs to every MST. But deleting e leaves edges 02 and 12, which connect 0–2–1. Hence e is not a bridge and therefore cannot be a minimum-weight bridge.
